findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so database storage and any snapshots are written in cleartext. Sensitive application data is exposed if the underlying storage or a snapshot is accessed or shared.

publicly_accessible = true gives the MySQL instance an internet-routable endpoint (also exported via the db_endpoint output), so the database is reachable from untrusted networks and protected only by a static master password.

The master username is the predictable default 'admin' and the password comes from a Terraform variable that is stored in plaintext in state and is interpolated into EC2 user data, exposing the database master credential.

findings.issue_category: no IAM auth or TLS enforcement
findings.description: IAM database authentication is not enabled and the attached parameter group does not set require_secure_transport, so authentication rests solely on a static password and clients may connect to this internet-facing database without TLS.

The user_data script embeds the RDS master username and plaintext password into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by any process or SSRF-capable web app on the host and is visible via the EC2 API/console.

No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled on an instance running a PHP web application; an SSRF can retrieve both the instance role credentials and the plaintext database secrets in user data.

No root_block_device encryption is configured, so the EBS root volume holding the database credential include file (/var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc) is stored unencrypted unless account-level default EBS encryption happens to apply.

The inline role policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the instance role. Combined with the internet-facing PHP application and IMDSv1, compromise of the host yields near-total control of S3, EC2 and RDS in the account, enabling data exfiltration and privilege escalation.

Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the RDS security group, allowing unrestricted outbound traffic that facilitates data exfiltration or command-and-control from a compromised resource.
